Also, the first murder investigation has that thing where something is painfully obvious but your idiot character has to have five conversations to finally put 2+2 together.

THE GOOD: Characters turn out to be quite charming when you get to know them.
The story is satisfyingly insane.
The investigation and Class Court mechanics are pretty satisfying.
You adjust the difficulty of puzzles and the difficulty of the arcade parts separately.

All in all I had a good time playing it.

It's a lot of tapping to get through the dialogue and the auto tap takes a little long to move onto the next one. Overall though, this was my only complain. The story was extremely intriguing and even after knowing what was going to happened at the end (the games been out for like a decade), it was still a fun play through and you have your own choices on who to speak with and who to hang out with. The gameplay was kind of confusing to understand but it came like second nature once it did click. I loved this game a lot, the story is awesome and has you wondering who's next. I highly recommend it if you like murder mysteries, suspense novels and cute NPC interactions.

I came into this expecting a wild murder mystery with interactive courtroom mechanics. What I got was hours of slow, repetitive, often infuriatingly padded dialogue, endless clicking through shallow character exposition, and a whole lot of “talk to this person again after doing something else so the story can progress” busywork.

When the game finally lets you investigate and engage in a class trial, it becomes something genuinely cool—clever, stylish, and fun. But the pacing up to that point is brutal. The game takes forever to get to the point, and even after the murder, you're stuck in more cutscenes and forced dialogue loops before the actual gameplay starts.

I understand why people love it, but for me, the ratio of fun to filler is completely off.
If you value your time and patience, know that the first 3–4 hours feel like you're being held hostage by anime dialogue before you're allowed to play the game everyone talks about.

Not for me.

I'm not usually into visual novels because I don't want to be judged for playing a visual novel like doki doki literature club or nekopara on the account of sexiness plus, I plan on playing my games on a flat screen and I share my room with my brother and I'll leave it up to you to imagine how it would go down...

on the other hand... danganronpa trigger happy havoc is a game I had my eyes on because the trailer looked awesome and there is so many anime and pop culture references in this game.... especially dragon ball z references pasted all over this game... if you love murder mystery solving with that 12 people mystery gang who ironically kill each other just so they can graduate high school, references, funny moments, cool cutscenes, awesome mini games, 2D art and more... you will love the danganronpa series.

Basically if Ace Attorney was a death game headed by cocky bloodthirsty teenagers.

The game may present itself as dark but.... there's pink blood, a talking demon bear, and you are following puberty driven teens. The story and mystery are both very fun though, and pair nicely with the surreal setting and presentation.

Otherwise gameplay is split into two halves (both visual novel based). Firstly, you have interactions with characters of your choice (building bonds with the characters you like before they probably die), and otherwise you have court trials (where you kill the friend who just killed your other friend....) Also you may find some of the characters are annoying.... so just vibe with the good ones while they last, and watch the most annoying ones not die.
The game that started it all. What is there to say that hasn't been said? An absolutely excellent visual novel for any level of interest and experience in the medium.

Nothing short of brilliant from the masterful story-telling which left question after question with no predictable answers to the well developed characters, Love em' or hate them (Looking at you hifumi) which enticed you into an amazing story with a painful cliffhanger. A story full of so many mysteries and questions it basically leaves you with no choice but to continue playing and ultimately buy the sequels, which I can ensure you I will definitely be playing in the near future.

Overall, I would without a doubt recommend this brilliant game to anyone who wants to be challenged with mystery and are appealed by the idea of story given games which I can ensure you this title provides plenty of. From the soundtracks to the storytelling, every scene and feature is EXECUTED with great thought and intent, Although the only visual novel I have ever played through, I can guarantee there won't be any others quite as great as Danganrompa.

Never have I been so extremely pleased with a video game series other than Danganronpa. Truly an excellent game that makes you use logic and puzzle-solving skills to develop relationships with many of the unique and talented students show to you. Danganronpa is a mystery game about 15 students trapped in a school: how do you get out? By killing a student and getting away with it. What happens if you get caught? A cinematic execution regarding your talent of course! This game uses horror, psychological, and emotional dialogue to its advantage alongside a humorous antagonist known as Monokuma. Although I am biased I would recommend this game! Even if you do not like it to its maximum potential, the second game is a large step up in difficulty and story with possibly the most complex yet intriguing baseline I have ever experienced. Pros: Art Style/Puzzles/Gameplay/FreeTimeEvents. Cons: Sometimes the answer is extremely obvious while other times it is too obscure for words. What would I rate this game? I would give it a 7.9/10 Is it worth the money? In my opinion yees, replayability is high and fun. Hope this helps!

I should have written a review for this game ages ago, I tell ya. Either way though, this game is an absolute must-play for fans of mystery stories with an open mind.

The characters intentionally seem like the ultimate stereotypes at first glance, but I promise you every single last one of them is astonishingly well developed. Nobody is left out here and everyone is given the amount of screen-time which they deserve.

The music is also spectacular. It has a very Rock/EDM feel to it, gives me hella vibes when trying to figure out who the hell the killer is.

The presentation is also fantastic, with an intuitive interface that is easy to learn and graphics which complement the game rather than bring it down.

On all fronts, this game deserves every ounce of praise it gets. The story and characters in this game are something every gamer should experience blind at some point. If you're looking for a fantastic story to dive into, look no further than Danganronpa!

Bought this on sale around Christmas in 2016 on a whim. Each time I saw it in my steam library, I made a sour face. What was I thinking?I never wanted to play Danganronpa. It looked stupid. Stupid bear, stupid pink blood. Now I'm kicking myself for not getting around to it earlier!

I didn't actually get around to playing it until late July/Early August 2017 but it's been my life since then pretty much. Is it flawed? Yes. But without a doubt I would reccomend it to anyone, it's a surprisingly approachable game for a visual novel as it doesn't necessarily feel like one after awhile. The visual novel part gets you comfortable before the wild ride of investigations and trials begin that bring new gameplay elements each time.

As a whole I'd say Danganronpa is an engaging and engrossing series of media with a lot to say. It can be surprisingly elegant and intelligent, though at the same time certain scenes have all the grace and subtlety of an axe to the head. Every spinoff, every sequel, every anime, I can reccomend without a doubt. And Trigger Happy Havoc is the start of all that.

More than anything, Danganronpa provokes strong reactions. Personally? I'm still upset, I'm still angry and I'm still in love with this game.

As a huge DanganRonpa fan (Played the PSP fan translation, played all 3 games in the series on the PS Vita, and own 2 copies of each game) I'm gonna keep it short for those who are considering this game.

If you enjoy a good murder mystery in lieu of Phoenix Wright, this is the game for you. It's a fantastic PC port with a fantastic cast of colourful characters with beautiful artwork, as well as music from Akira Yamaoka (Silent Hill Series) himself. But fair warning, you will go through a buttload of emotional trauma from the emotional connections you make with characters who may or may not end up dying. This game left me with some inner turmoil for a short while.

In addition, I'm hoping they can bring over the Zero Escape series over to Steam, as the games are from Spike Chunsoft as well and exceed in quality and story just as well as DanganRonpa does.

I currently am halfway though the 3rd chapter, and I have enjoyed every second of it.

I usually do not watch TV shows about police investigations, and I don't read any books revolving around investigations because I usually guess who the guilty person is about halfway through 90% of the time. I was expecting this game to be no exception, that is what made me hesitate a lot before buying it, but honestly, this VN has unpredictable plot twists.

You will constantly be on the edge of your seat wondering who and how killed a certain character, and when there are no murders you constantly wonder about how "The Mastermind" is going to try to get under the character's skin and make them commit murder. You should definitely buy this. If you are hesitant about buying it, don't be. It is on sale and I believe it would not have bothered me to have paid full price for this game.

After completing every achievement in the game, I can say for certain this game is the start to something fantastic. While the game itself is fine, comparing it to the other games is just unfair. But ignoring the other games, it's story is very slowly paced at times, but a very fun story overall. What the game does differently than most visual novels is put effort into actual gameplay as well, and I find that pretty neat. It adds a sense of suspense and a break from the typical dialogue, which can be very refreshing. If you want a full experience, you can also play School Mode, a mode unlocked after completing the story. It's a cute little resource management minigame with a bunch of cute dialogue from the cast, each with their own ending if you become besties with them. Albeit a grind, fans of the game should try it out! Either way, W game, would play again but Danganronpa v2 exists LMAO

Danganronpa's fanbase preceded the game itself and turned me off from playing it for years. When I played it myself, I was quite surprised to discover that it is actually really fun! The mysteries are written pretty well and most of the dialogue (which is most of the game) kept me eager to read more because it would be funny, progress the plot, or offer clues useful for solving a future mystery. That being said, a non-negligible chunk of the dialogue was pretty cringe, commonly featuring immature jokes about boners, boobs, "doing it", off color kinks, etc. Sometimes this stuff was so bad it got a laugh out of me, but plenty of it did nothing but make me embarrassed to be playing this game, so I can see this making the game much less appealing to some people.

If you can handle some cringe dialogue and enjoy other visual novels/text focused games I would really recommend playing this game, despite whatever impression its fanbase may have left on you!

The whole Danganronpa series is fun to play through, from the plot that it conjures, to the main details outlined in the description of the game. The gameplay style is somewhat similar to the genre that Phoenix Wright and Professor Layton are categorized in, but it takes a fairly different approach by creating some brand new methods that are unique to Danganronpa. I won' t necessarily discuss what the main gameplay is like, because I would most likely spoil the plot of some chapters, but all I can say is that it is best to start this game without watching any playthroughs (if you would actually like to play it), or without looking up certain phrases online because there are a load of surprises found within the Danganronpa games that are best to be experienced without awareness of these surprises eventually occurring. One last thing I want to add is that the characters and their development throughout the game are planned perfectly with the progression of the game.

Danganronpa: Trigger Happy Havoc is a game full of unexpected plot twists, tedious (yet rewarding) crime scene investigations, and some of the most insane characters ever

What I like most about Danganronpa is that it requires the player to pay attention to minute details surrounding the crime scene, all of which are necessary to pass the class trials.

At its core, Danganronpa is a captivating "whodunit" game coupled with a rich storyline. It is a game totally worth buying and 100% exceeds its point-and-click game mechanic

This game successfully broke and filled me with despair. :,) I love this game and will probably never get over certain characters + how things ended (to be completely honest I was enraged with the games conclusion but after thinking about it more, I'm pretty sure that's exactly what they wanted).

Wonderful characters, art, soundtrack, story (I'd stream the game to others on Discord and even the ones who didn't care about Danganronpa got invested in the mysteries), the whole shebang. It's definitely not for everyone, but would recommend playing if you were already interested. Have fun watching your favs die!

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (96%): players love the story and characters, which most reviews praise.
The main complaint is the ending, which some players found disappointing.

details.text: Recent reviews raise complaints about the story and characters far less often than reviews do over all time.
Players who reviewed after very little play are far less positive than veterans, at 79% against 97% for the longest-playing group.
